scenes.anchor_text:
“Above silence, the illuminating storms—dying storms— illuminate the silence above.”
The above sample is noteworthy as it is a ketek, a complex form of holy Vorin poem.
scenes.scene_description: An abstract representation of the ketek, focusing on the interplay between illumination and silence.
scenes.image_prompt: Abstract watercolor, illuminating silence as a vibrant, ethereal glow, harmonious blend of light blues and whites contrasted with muted grays, soft, blended washes creating a sense of depth and mystery

scenes.anchor_text: The complete poem must form a sentence that is grammatically correct and  poignant in meaning. Because of the difficulty in constructing a ketek, the structure was once considered the highest and most impressive form of all Vorin poetry.
scenes.scene_description: The concept of complex and profound poetry represented abstractly.
scenes.image_prompt: Expressive abstract painting, complexity and profundity as intertwined lines, monochromatic shades of deep blues and purples, long flowing lines converging and diverging to show the poem, serene color wash

scenes.anchor_text: The fact that this one was uttered by an illiterate, dying Herdazian in a language he barely spoke should be of particular note. There is no record of this particular ketek in any repository of Vorin poetry, so it is very unlikely that the subject was merely repeating something he once heard.
scenes.scene_description: A representation of surprise and wonder at the origin of the ketek.
scenes.image_prompt: Abstract watercolor, revelation as sudden bloom, vibrant and saturated yellows and oranges emerging from muted browns and grays, short, energetic strokes indicating surprise, calm, horizontal strokes
